findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reclassify `transition`: verify transition_cli's actual text output (only `UNBLOCKED:` on close, `No transition needed` on noop, silent for non-close) and treat non-close transitions as GAINING a new confirmation line rather than normalizing an existing one, adjusting the AC-3 'every datum the old line carried' assertion accordingly.
evidence: Plan Scope: 'Verbs that already print (create, idea, revert, claim, transition, session-log) are NORMALIZED to the same message contract ... the line keeps every datum it prints today ... transitioned <alias>: <from> -> <to>'
src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:608-629: text mode prints only `No transition needed` (noop), `UNBLOCKED: ...` (when target_status=='closed'), and returns 0 with NO stdout for other transitions
search for `print(f"transitioned` returned no matches
findings.finding: The plan lists `transition` among 'Verbs that already print' and frames its normalization as keeping 'every datum it prints today ... transitioned <alias>: <from> -> <to>' with 'zero information loss'. But transition_cli in text mode does not print any transition-confirmation line for a non-close transition (open->in_progress etc.): it writes `UNBLOCKED: <ids>` only when target_status=='closed', `No transition needed` on the noop, and nothing otherwise. The from->to datum is therefore NOT emitted today for the common non-close case, so this is a NEW confirmation line rather than a normalization, and AC-3's 'test asserts the new line contains every datum the old line carried' has no old line to compare against for those transitions.
findings.location: Scope ('Verbs that already print (... transition ...) are NORMALIZED') and AC line 3
scenarios: An open->in_progress transition: today prints nothing; the plan's 'normalization' framing implies an existing line to preserve
AC-3 test for transition tries to assert 'new line contains every datum the old line carried' but there is no old line for non-close transitions

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct step 3's file references: `_REGISTRY` (comment/tag/untag/archive/set-verify-commands), the `_split_positionals` usage-error guard, `_ARGV_REGISTRY`, and the per-verb `parse_output` handling live in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` (the leaf-write `main()`), not `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py`; state whether pre-extraction goes in the top-level router, in `_commands.main`, or both, and how the two layers coordinate.
evidence: Plan: 'the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaf verbs (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands)' ... 'src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py'

src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:359-363 dispatches `_WRITES_FULL` verbs via `commands_main([sub, *rest])` into `rebar._commands.main`, confirming _REGISTRY/parse_output live a layer below
findings.finding: Step 3 names the positional-only `_REGISTRY` leaf verbs (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) as living at `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:125`, but `_REGISTRY` — containing exactly those five verbs — is defined in `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py:41`. The `_cli/__init__.py` reference at :125 is `_WRITES_FULL`, a different frozenset. The `_split_positionals` usage-error guard the plan cites ('treat any option-looking token as a usage error'), `_ARGV_REGISTRY` (the self-parsers for set-file-impact/attach-commits/create/edit/link/unlink/revert/session-log), the per-verb `parse_output` handling to be promoted, and the leaf-write `main()` all live in `_commands/__init__.py`, one dispatch layer below the top-level router.
findings.location: Plan step 3 ('Global output flags pre-extracted at the top-level router (src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py)')
scenarios: Executor implements top-level pre-extraction in _cli/__init__.py but the usage-error guard and parse_output promotion targets are in _commands/__init__.py, causing either duplicated/misplaced logic or an incomplete change.
findings.suggested_fix: Relocate the step-3 references to `src/rebar/_commands/__init__.py` for `_REGISTRY`/`_split_positionals`/`_ARGV_REGISTRY`/`parse_output`, and clarify that `_cli/__init__.py` only forwards `_WRITES_FULL` verbs via `commands_main([sub, *rest])`; decide the single argv-stripping seam that both the leaf `_REGISTRY` path and the `_ARGV_REGISTRY` self-parsers pass through (e.g. `_commands.main` before dispatch).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile add_dependency's existing stdout REDIRECT-record print with the new confirmation: fold the redirect into the confirmation line (text) / mutation envelope (json) as a field, so stdout stays a single line (text) or single document (json).
evidence: src/rebar/graph/_links.py:220-224 print(json.dumps(redirect_record)) with T201 noqa 'stdout data ... (CLI contract)'
src/rebar/graph/_links.py:276 _emit_redirect() on the no-op path; line ~end of write path also emits
Plan step 4: 'stdout remains exclusively the JSON document; the outcome rides as a structured field'
findings.finding: add_dependency already prints its REDIRECT record as raw JSON to stdout (_emit_redirect, called on both the write and no-op paths). The plan does not reconcile this pre-existing stdout emission with the new text confirmation line (text mode gets mixed line + JSON) nor with step 4's guarantee that under --output json stdout is 'exclusively the JSON document' (a redirected link would emit the redirect JSON AND the mutation envelope = two documents).
scenarios: rebar link with a redirect in default mode -> stdout has both a JSON redirect record and the text 'linked ...' line
rebar link --output json with a redirect -> two JSON objects on stdout
findings.suggested_fix: Have the CLI layer own the redirect display (via the seam's return value) and suppress add_dependency's own _emit_redirect at the CLI seam, so the redirect becomes a field of the confirmation/envelope rather than a second stdout emission.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the link/unlink confirmation line reflects hierarchy REDIRECT: derive the printed endpoints from the seam's resolved edge (or the returned REDIRECT record), not solely from CLI args, so a promoted write is reported accurately.
evidence: Plan step 1: 'built ONLY from CLI arguments + the write seam's outcome' and line form 'linked <src> -> <target> (<relation>)'
src/rebar/graph/_links.py:195-218 resolves resolved_source/resolved_target and builds a REDIRECT record when was_redirected
add_dependency docstring (line 167-172): 'Returns the REDIRECT record when hierarchy escalation moved either endpoint'
findings.finding: The link success line is spec'd as built 'ONLY from CLI arguments,' but add_dependency performs hierarchy promotion that can redirect the written edge to resolved_source->resolved_target (different from the CLI args). A CLI-arg-only confirmation line would misreport the actual write in the redirect case, defeating the plan's own purpose of letting agents trust the confirmation instead of re-reading.
findings.location: Plan step 1 (link confirmation line) & step 2 (add_dependency contract)
scenarios: rebar link A B blocks where A or B is promoted to a higher tier — the durable edge is between the promoted ids, but the confirmation prints the unpromoted CLI args
findings.suggested_fix: In step 1/2, state that when add_dependency reports a redirect, the confirmation uses the resolved endpoints (e.g. 'linked <resolved_src> -> <resolved_tgt> (<relation>) [redirected from <src> -> <tgt>]'); the seam's existing REDIRECT return already carries this.
